summary: An excerpt from a novel (labeled Book 10, part 11) in which Posy, a neighbor, talks with Lawrence about the city's surveillance and the guilt everyone accumulates, citing a sofa bought off a cop, overriding a heating governor, and a neighbor family taken away after a tattoo was seen. Lawrence, who investigates data anomalies, is rebuffed when he asks what this has to do with the Order, and leaves after she tells him to find his escapee. The passage closes with a background sketch of Zbigniew Krotoski, a New Yorker inducted into the Order four years earlier who spent his early years provoking pointless flamewars about working for the Securitat.
one_line: In a fiction excerpt, Posy tells Lawrence that everyone is guilty of something in a surveilled city, then Lawrence learns background on fugitive Zbigniew Krotoski.
key_facts: Posy points out an apartment building across the way with broken windows covered in cardboard, saying the residents were taken away last week.
Posy says that when people become persons of interest they are taken away and later authorities always find a reason to keep them away.
Lawrence finds stuff that doesn't belong in the data and says he doesn't arrest people.
Posy says, "We're all guilty of something, Lawrence. That's how the game is rigged."
Posy says she bought a sofa from a cop ten years ago when he was leaving the building, without a receipt and without tax collected.
Posy says she overrode the governor on her radiator ten minutes after it was installed, by sticking a penny between two contacts.
Posy says the city makes overriding the heating governor easy because it expects everyone to do it, so once everyone has, everyone is guilty.
Posy describes a neighboring family, possibly Pakistani, Sri Lankan or Bangladeshi, whose wife she saw at the service laundry carrying kids to or from day-care.
Posy saw a number tattooed on the wife's wrist when her sleeve rode up while she reached for change.
Posy says the wife pounded on the window and screamed for help when the family, including her husband and kids, was taken.
Posy tells Lawrence he is not very good at connecting the dots for someone who is supposed to know himself.
Lawrence thanks Posy, puts his glass in the sink, and she tells him, "Take care out there," and "Good luck finding your escapee."
Lawrence knows Zbigniew Krotoski was inducted into the Order four years earlier.
Zbigniew Krotoski is a native-born New Yorker.
In his first two years in the Order, Krotoski tried to coax elders into pointless flamewars about the ethics of working for the Securitat.
